playbooks.title: Robotic system not responding with AGVs stopped or out of sync
playbooks.user_facing_summary: Use this troubleshooting flow when a site reports that robotic operation has stopped, AGVs are not moving or are out of sync, small sort activity has stopped, or the RMS view is blank or abnormal. Confirm the observable system state, inspect service and application evidence, recover the affected service or gateway through an authorized procedure, correct residual AGV state, and validate both service responsiveness and resumed operation.
playbooks.playbook_goal: Determine whether the site-wide stoppage is associated with an abnormal OptiSweep, WCSWebApplication, or related gateway state; support authorized recovery; identify residual AGV synchronization or state issues; and confirm stable robotic operation before release.
observed_entry_symptoms: Nothing is moving across the site or bots are stopped in multiple areas.
The robotic system is reported as not responding.
Small sort operation is not running.
AGVs are reported out of sync or several AGVs stop after a heartbeat issue.
Totes cannot be removed from the hospital workflow.
RMS or HMI is mostly blank or displays an apparent ".NET Control not created." message.
The site reports no obvious failed AGV even though automated movement has stopped.
support_user_language_examples: We can't get totes out of hospital
Several bots stopped after a heartbeat issue
Nothing is moving across the site or bots
The robotic system is reported as not responding
Small sort operation is not running
AGVs are reported out of sync or several
Totes cannot be removed from the hospital workflow
RMS or HMI is mostly blank or displays
The site reports no obvious failed AGV even
affected_systems_or_components: Windows Event Viewer / Service Control Manager
playbooks.confidence_reason: The packet provides clear observable entry symptoms, named diagnostic surfaces, a source-supported service failure signal, a high-level recovery sequence, residual AGV correction, and multiple validation signals. Exact root cause and the significance of some memory and RMS messages remain uncertain.

nodes.title: Confirm the stoppage pattern and abnormal control-system presentation
nodes.intent: Determine whether the report represents a broad robotic-operation stoppage with an abnormal RMS or HMI presentation rather than an isolated AGV issue.
nodes.goal: Determine whether the report represents a broad robotic-operation stoppage with an abnormal RMS or HMI presentation rather than an isolated AGV issue.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to confirm with the site whether the affected zone or workflow has broad loss of movement, whether small sort or hospital handling is also stopped, and whether RMS/HMI shows a populated normal status view or a blank/control-not-created presentation. Use generic affected-zone and reported-robot questioning rather than incident-specific identifiers.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source reports a site-wide or multi-area motion stoppage, no obvious failed AGV, stopped small sort, hospital tote-removal difficulty, and abnormal RMS/HMI presentation.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to confirm with the site whether the affected zone or workflow has broad loss of movement, whether small sort or hospital handling is also stopped, and whether RMS/HMI shows a populated normal status view or a blank/control-not-created presentation. Use generic affected-zone and reported-robot questioning rather than incident-specific identifiers.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site or operator confirms whether the affected area has broad loss of movement, whether the small sort or hospital workflow is also affected, and whether RMS/HMI is blank or shows an abnormal control message. In RMS/HMI, a healthy or alternate pattern is normal populated system status with localized impact only; an unhealthy pattern is broad stopped operation with blank or abnormal system presentation; inconclusive means the scope, affected workflow, or displayed message cannot be confirmed.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The packet supports determining overall fleet or system-down versus running state from the site report and abnormal RMS overview.
The packet includes reports of stopped bots and visible RMS system/AGV error sections, although no readable specific error rows were extracted.

ontology_gaps: No supplied mapping establishes the operational meaning of the apparent ".NET Control not created." message.
healthy_indicators: Site reports movement continuing normally or impact limited to one asset.
RMS/HMI displays populated normal operational content.
Small sort and hospital workflow are operating normally.
unhealthy_indicators: Nothing is moving across multiple areas.
Small sort is stopped or totes cannot be removed from hospital.
RMS/HMI is mostly blank or displays the apparent control-not-created message.
inconclusive_indicators: Only one robot or one local area is affected.
The RMS message cannot be read or its operational meaning is uncertain.
The site cannot confirm whether the issue is still active.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Reports state that 4-6 bots were not moving, totes could not be removed from hospital, and the site reported nothing was moving.
RMS page appears mostly blank and shows '.NET Control not created.'
Work order states that the robotic system was not responding and the small sort was not running.

nodes.primary_action: Confirm whether the stoppage is broad (multi-area) and whether RMS/HMI presentation is blank or shows an abnormal/control-not-created message; otherwise switch to localized/alternate symptom triage.
evidence_to_collect: Site confirmation of scope: broad vs localized loss of movement/robot operation
Whether small sort operation is stopped
Whether hospital workflow is impacted (e.g., totes cannot be removed)
RMS/HMI presentation: populated normal status view vs mostly blank / abnormal message (e.g., '.NET Control not created.')
Whether the site can confirm the problem is still active
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Site confirms movement continues normally or impact is limited to a single asset/local area, and RMS/HMI shows a populated normal status view for the overall fleet (localized impact only).
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Nothing is moving across multiple areas; small sort is stopped and/or hospital totes cannot be removed; RMS/HMI is mostly blank or displays an abnormal/control-not-created style presentation that matches a system-level stoppage pattern.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Only one robot/local area appears affected, or the RMS message cannot be read/its meaning is uncertain, or the site cannot reliably confirm whether the issue is still active.

optional_corroboration.note: Treat the apparent RMS message (e.g., '.NET Control not created.') as an observed symptom, not a confirmed diagnosis. Prefer corroborating scope and operational impact with site interview questions.

nodes.generated_guidance: Ask the site/operator to confirm (1) how many areas/robots are affected, (2) whether small sort and hospital handling are also stopped, and (3) whether RMS/HMI shows populated overall status versus blank/abnormal presentation. Use these confirmations to branch into system-level service/application evidence review (broad) versus retriage for localized/alternate causes (not broad).

ontology_evidence.title: Capability — Fleet / overall system status
ontology_evidence.text: Capability fleet_system_status: Confirm overall fleet / system-down vs running from overview surfaces.. When: Blank RMS, site-wide stoppage report, overall system page down. Not for: Single-AGV active error deep dive without overall context.. Surfaces: rms_ui, aveva_hmi, event_viewer, wcs_sql, site_interview. Support contract: {}. Backend mappings: []. DBs: robotics, sorter_sweeper. Models: SystemDatabaseModel, SystemStateModel, SortModel. APIs: SystemState. Key fields: SystemDatabaseModel.Id: R

ontology_evidence.title: Capability — AGV active errors
ontology_evidence.text: Capability agv_active_errors: Confirm whether AGVs/robots currently have active error or fault state.. When: Site reports AGV stopped, alarms, bump, path lost, or software showing robot faults; corroborate RMS overview vs WCS truth. Not for: Physical bump recovery steps (use agv_physical_recovery); Ignition OPC alone; tote NoRead.. Surfaces: rms_ui, wcs_sql, wcs_api, site_interview, apidog. Support contract: {}. Backend mappings: []. DBs: robotics, sorter_sweeper. Models: AgvActiveErrorDatabaseM

ontology_evidence.title: Capability — AGV physical recovery / removal
ontology_evidence.text: Capability agv_physical_recovery: Coordinate on-site AGV add/remove/bump recovery with system-side roster repair.. When: Floor recovery, bump codes, motionless robot handling, remove/add AGV. Not for: SQL-only active error query without floor action when physical recovery is required.. Surfaces: physical_floor, rms_ui, wcs_api, site_interview, apidog. Support contract: {}. Backend mappings: []. DBs: robotics. Models: . APIs: RemoveAgv, RecoverAGV, GetAGVStatuses. Key fields: . Activities: site_i

nodes.intent: Use the available Windows log evidence to determine whether OptiSweep or WCSWebApplication entered an abnormal state near the onset of the operational stoppage.
nodes.goal: Use the available Windows log evidence to determine whether OptiSweep or WCSWebApplication entered an abnormal state near the onset of the operational stoppage.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to inspect Windows Event Viewer System and Application logs for OptiSweep Service Control Manager termination events and clustered WCSWebApplication or Application Error entries, and to correlate their timing with the reported stoppage without inferring root cause from the event alone.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source contains Event Viewer evidence of OptiSweep termination, clustered WCSWebApplication errors, a failed database command, and a later OptiSweep Running state.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to inspect Windows Event Viewer System and Application logs for OptiSweep Service Control Manager termination events and clustered WCSWebApplication or Application Error entries, and to correlate their timing with the reported stoppage without inferring root cause from the event alone.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: L1/L2 support observes Windows Event Viewer System and Application logs. An unhealthy pattern is an OptiSweep Service Control Manager termination event or clustered WCSWebApplication/Application Error entries near the stoppage; a healthy or alternate pattern is no corresponding service or application failure, prompting another investigation; inconclusive means logs are unavailable, timestamps cannot be correlated, or event details are incomplete.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The packet directly shows Windows Event Viewer and Windows Services evidence for OptiSweep termination and service state.
The packet reports OptiSweep service failure and WCSWebApplication errors, supporting service-health investigation without confirming a definitive cause.
The packet shows clustered WCSWebApplication errors and a failed database command in the Application log.

ontology_gaps: The supplied ontology does not establish a backend mapping for the specific WCSWebApplication Event 20102 evidence.
healthy_indicators: No relevant service termination or clustered application errors are found near the symptom onset.
OptiSweep is running and no corresponding abnormal event is present.
The evidence points to an alternate subsystem rather than the named service/application path.
unhealthy_indicators: Event Viewer shows OptiSweep Event 7031 stating that the service terminated unexpectedly.
Application log shows clustered WCSWebApplication or Application Error entries near the reported stoppage.
A WCSWebApplication Event 20102 reports a failed database command.
inconclusive_indicators: Only a current Running state is available without historical timing.
Logs are unavailable or event details are unreadable.
The events are present but cannot be correlated with the operational symptom.

nodes.primary_action: Inspect Windows Event Viewer and Windows Services evidence to determine whether OptiSweep termination or clustered WCSWebApplication/Application Error events correlate with the stoppage onset.

evidence_to_collect: Windows Event Viewer System log evidence for OptiSweep Service Control Manager termination/unexpected restarts (e.g., 7031 pattern)

nodes.healthy_interpretation: No relevant OptiSweep termination or correlated clustered WCSWebApplication/Application Error evidence near symptom onset; or only current Running state without abnormal correlation (prompt alternate investigation).
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: OptiSweep unexpectedly terminated/restarted and/or WCSWebApplication clustered errors/failures are present near the stoppage onset timestamps, supporting a correlated service/application investigation path.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Logs unavailable, timestamps cannot be correlated, or event details are incomplete/unreadable; only a current Running state is available without historical timing.

optional_corroboration.note: Correlate by timestamps to the site-reported stoppage onset; do not infer root cause from events alone.

nodes.title: Check whether Ignition gateway health is abnormal or merely a related observation
nodes.intent: Determine whether the Ignition gateway shows a current responsiveness problem or whether the memory observation is only follow-up context.
nodes.goal: Determine whether the Ignition gateway shows a current responsiveness problem or whether the memory observation is only follow-up context.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to inspect the Ignition gateway Systems Overview for gateway responsiveness, current response behavior, recent slow-response events, and available CPU or memory trend evidence, while treating unlabeled trend changes as inconclusive unless correlated with a confirmed failure.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source includes requests to determine whether Ignition crashed, memory trend charts, an Ignition Systems Overview showing 11 ms response and no recent slow-response events, and a note that memory did not indicate it caused a crash.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to inspect the Ignition gateway Systems Overview for gateway responsiveness, current response behavior, recent slow-response events, and available CPU or memory trend evidence, while treating unlabeled trend changes as inconclusive unless correlated with a confirmed failure.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: L1/L2 support observes the Ignition Systems Overview and available memory or CPU trend evidence. A healthy signal is a responding gateway with a current response time and no recent slow-response events; an unhealthy signal is an unavailable or nonresponsive gateway or a clearly abnormal resource trend correlated with the stoppage; inconclusive means the snapshot is stale, the trend lacks labels, or the gateway state cannot be verified.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The packet directly shows an Ignition gateway Systems Overview with response and slow-response indicators.

ontology_gaps: The supplied evidence does not identify the meaning of the memory chart reference line or provide a validated causal threshold.
healthy_indicators: Ignition Systems Overview responds and shows a current response time.
Recent Slow Response Events shows no events to display.
Memory trend is described as looking better and remains below the visible reference line.
unhealthy_indicators: Ignition gateway cannot be reached or does not respond.
Recent slow-response activity or other gateway health indicators are clearly abnormal.
A resource trend is visibly abnormal and temporally correlates with the operational failure.
inconclusive_indicators: A memory trend changes sharply without a labeled threshold or causal evidence.
The snapshot has no reliable timestamp or is not clearly from the affected gateway.
The gateway responds normally after the incident but historical state cannot be reconstructed.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Support stated that the memory trend did not indicate that memory caused a crash and suggested checking CPU trend.
Ignition Systems Overview shows current response time 11 ms and no recent slow-response events.
Memory trend remains below a higher visible reference line without an obvious threshold crossing.

nodes.primary_action: Check whether the Ignition gateway shows current responsiveness/health abnormalities versus treating the memory observation as follow-up context.
evidence_to_collect: Ignition Systems Overview response behavior and current response time
Recent Slow Response Events indicator (presence/absence of events)
Any gateway health indicators that show current unavailability/non-responsiveness
Interpret unlabeled memory trend changes as inconclusive unless they correlate with a confirmed failure in gateway responsiveness
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Ignition Systems Overview responds with current response time; no recent slow-response events displayed; resource trend not visibly abnormal or described as improving below reference.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Ignition gateway cannot be reached or does not respond; recent slow-response activity/health indicators are clearly abnormal and correlated with stoppage timing.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Memory/trend changes are sharp but unlabeled thresholds/causal rules absent; snapshot is stale/unclear; or gateway state cannot be verified (e.g., after recovery it appears normal but historical evidence is missing).

optional_corroboration.note: Do not claim memory caused the crash; treat it as follow-up context unless gateway health indicators confirm a correlated failure.

nodes.generated_guidance: Use the Ignition Systems Overview snapshot to determine whether there is a current gateway responsiveness problem. If unhealthy/unreachable, proceed to authorized gateway/service recovery (node_4). If healthy/unhealthy correlation is absent, still proceed to recovery because the OptiSweep termination evidence remains relevant (node_4), per the workflow branching hints.

nodes.goal: Identify whether AGVs remain out of sync, unmapped, or otherwise abnormal after the service or gateway recovery.

nodes.source_supported_description: After the OptiSweep reset, the source says RMS was used to locate and fix out-of-sync AGVs one by one. The packet also includes RMS map and SSMS state evidence.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to inspect the RMS fleet or map view for residual out-of-sync, unavailable, unmapped, or abnormal-state AGVs after service recovery, using generic asset identification and state-correction criteria. nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The operator or support role observes the RMS fleet/map state and, when authorized, corroborates with the source-supported AGV state evidence. A healthy signal is a normal fleet view with expected AGV participation and no residual synchronization issue; an unhealthy signal is one or more AGVs remaining out of sync or in an abnormal state after recovery; inconclusive means the roster, map, or state cannot be reliably read.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The source describes locating individual out-of-sync AGVs and includes RMS map and backend state evidence.
The packet contains AGV error sections and reports of stopped or out-of-sync AGVs, but no readable individual error codes.
Residual AGV state must be evaluated in the context of restored fleet operation.

ontology_gaps: The packet does not establish which displayed AGV states are abnormal versus expected for the current workflow.
The packet does not provide a validated mapping from the SSMS state values to a correction decision.
healthy_indicators: RMS shows the expected fleet and no residual out-of-sync indicators.
AGV state and location presentation are consistent with restored operation.
No unresolved AGV error or mapping anomaly remains visible.
unhealthy_indicators: RMS identifies AGVs as out of sync or otherwise abnormal after service recovery.
AGV roster, location, or map state is inconsistent with expected operation.
The site still observes stopped assets after the service has recovered.
inconclusive_indicators: RMS is unavailable or remains blank.
The displayed state is readable but its operational meaning is not established.
Only a single AGV snapshot is available without confirmation of fleet-wide state.

nodes.healthy_interpretation: RMS shows expected fleet state; no residual out-of-sync indicators; AGV state/locations consistent with restored operation.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: One or more AGVs remain out of sync or in an abnormal state after recovery; RMS roster/map/state inconsistent with expected operation; assets still appear stopped due to residual sync issues.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: RMS is unavailable/blank, displayed state is readable but operational meaning is not established, or only a single AGV snapshot without fleet-wide confirmation.

optional_corroboration.note: If residual sync problems are suspected but RMS is unreadable, corroborate with WCS/Helix DB (SSMS) AGV state inspection evidence where accessible.

nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed for authorized RMS-based correction of an identified out-of-sync or abnormal AGV state, including safety prerequisites, asset-selection controls, role limits, and criteria for stopping before any physical AGV recovery. Exact historical correction steps are intentionally left to the procedure layer.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source reports that RMS was used to locate and fix out-of-sync AGVs after the OptiSweep reset, but it does not provide a complete reusable procedure.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed for authorized RMS-based correction of an identified out-of-sync or abnormal AGV state, including safety prerequisites, asset-selection controls, role limits, and criteria for stopping before any physical AGV recovery. Exact historical correction steps are intentionally left to the procedure layer.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: An authorized role records that the identified AGV state correction has completed. Progress is indicated by the affected AGV returning to an expected state and no longer blocking fleet operation; failure is indicated by persistent abnormal state or repeated loss of synchronization; inconclusive means the correction outcome cannot be observed.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The source supports correction of residual AGV state identified through RMS.

ontology_gaps: The packet does not specify the approved correction mechanism or distinguish software correction from physical recovery.
healthy_indicators: The affected AGV presents the expected state after authorized correction.
Fleet operation can proceed without the same synchronization anomaly recurring immediately.
unhealthy_indicators: The AGV remains out of sync or returns to an abnormal state.
Correction would require an unsupported or unsafe action.
Multiple assets remain affected beyond the supported correction scope.
inconclusive_indicators: RMS does not refresh or the resulting state cannot be observed.
The source-supported correction path does not identify the affected asset clearly.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: Do not substitute physical AGV handling, E-stop, or configuration changes for this node. Stop if the approved RMS correction scope or safety preconditions are not clear.

nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: RMS does not refresh; resulting state cannot be observed; affected asset not clearly identified in the correction path.

nodes.title: Validate service responsiveness, AGV status, and resumed operation
nodes.intent: Confirm that the recovered service and fleet state support stable automated operation before declaring the troubleshooting path complete.
nodes.goal: Confirm that the recovered service and fleet state support stable automated operation before declaring the troubleshooting path complete.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to validate OptiSweep responsiveness in Windows Services and through the source-evidenced GetAgvStatuses API client, inspect returned AGV status records, confirm RMS shows the expected fleet state, and obtain site confirmation that automated movement or auto bag-out has resumed. Treat an HTTP 200 response with a schema warning as partial evidence rather than complete recovery.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source provides Windows Services, GetAgvStatuses API, RMS follow-up, and site resumption evidence, while explicitly leaving the API schema warning and complete restoration scope uncertain.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to validate OptiSweep responsiveness in Windows Services and through the source-evidenced GetAgvStatuses API client, inspect returned AGV status records, confirm RMS shows the expected fleet state, and obtain site confirmation that automated movement or auto bag-out has resumed. Treat an HTTP 200 response with a schema warning as partial evidence rather than complete recovery.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: L1/L2 support observes the OptiSweep service state and the GetAgvStatuses API, while the site observes RMS and operational movement. Healthy recovery is supported by a responding OptiSweep service, a successful status response with returned AGV records, expected AGV status values, and site confirmation that automated operation or auto bag-out has resumed. Unhealthy recovery is continued no-response, repeated service failure, abnormal AGV state, or continued stoppage; inconclusive means HTTP success occurs but returned data cannot be interpreted, schema validation remains ambiguous, or site operation is not confirmed.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The packet directly shows a GetAgvStatuses API request returning HTTP 200 and records.
The source supports validating resumed fleet operation and site running state.
Returned AGV records and RMS review are used to assess residual fleet state.

ontology_gaps: The packet does not provide a validated interpretation of the API schema warning or a complete API-to-RMS state reconciliation rule.
healthy_indicators: OptiSweep is shown as Running.
GetAgvStatuses returns HTTP 200 and AGV records.
Returned records include expected normal-status values.
RMS no longer shows unresolved out-of-sync AGVs.
Site confirms automated movement or auto bag-out has resumed and remains stable.
unhealthy_indicators: GetAgvStatuses does not respond or returns no usable records.
OptiSweep is stopped or terminates again.
RMS still shows out-of-sync or abnormal AGVs.
The site remains stopped or cannot resume automated operation.
inconclusive_indicators: HTTP 200 is returned but the response schema warning prevents reliable interpretation.
The service is Running but the screenshot timing relative to recovery is unknown.
RMS or site confirmation is unavailable.
Auto bag-out resumes but broader fleet stability is not confirmed.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: GetAgvStatuses returned HTTP 200 with AGV records, including visible NORMAL values, but the API client reported a schema warning.
Windows Services shows OptiSweep Running.
After RMS correction of out-of-sync AGVs, the site resumed auto bag-out.

nodes.primary_action: Validate OptiSweep responsiveness and fleet state, then confirm stable resumed robotic operation with the site.
nodes.primary_surface: wcs_api (GetAgvStatuses) + windows_services state + rms_ui + site interview
evidence_to_collect: OptiSweep service state in Windows Services (Running)
GetAgvStatuses API response status (HTTP 200 expected) and returned AGV records
Returned AGV records show interpretable expected/normal-status values (treat schema warning as partial evidence only)
RMS fleet state returns to normal (no unresolved out-of-sync indicators)
Site confirmation that automated movement or auto bag-out has resumed and remains stable
nodes.healthy_interpretation: OptiSweep is Running; GetAgvStatuses returns usable HTTP 200 with returned AGV records; returned records are interpretable as normal/expected; RMS is normal; site confirms resumed stable operation.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: GetAgvStatuses fails/unusable; OptiSweep stopped/terminates again; RMS still shows abnormal out-of-sync AGVs; site cannot confirm resumed automated operation.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: HTTP 200 occurs but schema warning prevents reliable interpretation; service appears Running but timing vs recovery unclear; site confirmation unavailable; broader fleet stability not confirmed.

optional_corroboration.note: If schema warning blocks interpretation, corroborate using RMS fleet state and any additional evidence available (still treat as partial and do not declare full recovery).

nodes.generated_guidance: Combine service availability (Windows Services), API responsiveness (GetAgvStatuses), fleet state (RMS), and site operational confirmation. Require evidence consistency: HTTP success and visible NORMAL values are partial, not sufficient without interpretable returned values and site confirmation of resumed operations.

When: Site reports AGV stopped, alarms, bump, path lost, or software showing robot faults; corroborate RMS overview vs WCS truth. Not for: Physical bump recovery steps (use agv_physical_recovery); Ignition OPC alone; tote NoRead.. Surfaces: rms_ui, wcs_sql, wcs_api, site_interview, apidog. Support contract: {}. Backend mappings: []. DBs: robotics, sorter_sweeper. Models: AgvActiveErrorDatabaseM

nodes.diagnostic_interpretation: Completion gate for the troubleshooting flow; directs to success (end of playbook) or escalation gate when validation fails.

playbooks.title: Zone pairing failure with abnormal AMR routing or roster state
playbooks.user_facing_summary: Use when a site reports that a zone cannot obtain a pair, AMRs are not behaving as expected, or replacement AMRs are routing to the hospital instead of supporting the affected workflow.
playbooks.playbook_goal: Confirm the observable pairing and fleet symptoms, determine whether the affected AMR roster or mapping state is abnormal, guide an authorized site-side isolation or removal decision when supported, and validate that normal operation returns.
observed_entry_symptoms: A zone is unable to get a pair.
The ACB workflow is reported as down or unable to operate.
Replacement AMRs route to the hospital lane instead of supporting the affected zone.
An AMR is reported with low battery or is physically under a rack.
The site reports that AMR behavior remains abnormal after an attempted replacement.
support_user_language_examples: Nothing is pairing in the zone
AMRs are going to the hospital
The replacement robots keep going to hospital
We have a low-battery robot under the rack
The robots were removed and added but it still isn't working
The fleet is not taking tasks
A zone is unable to get a pair
The ACB workflow is reported as down or unable to operate
Replacement AMRs route to the hospital lane instead
An AMR is reported with low battery or
The site reports that AMR behavior remains abnormal after an attempted replacement
zone unable to get a pair
every AMR goes to the hospital
playbooks.confidence_reason: The packet contains a clear observable symptom pattern, a named RMS surface, repeated discussion of remove/add and mapping state, a source-supported site-side recovery action, and reported post-action stability. Confidence is limited because the RMS details are partly unreadable, the recovery was narrative rather than independently verified, and the source uses inconsistent ACB/ECB naming.

nodes.title: Confirm zone pairing failure and abnormal AMR behavior
nodes.intent: Determine whether the reported issue is an active zone pairing failure accompanied by abnormal AMR routing or inability to support the affected workflow.
nodes.goal: Determine whether the reported issue is an active zone pairing failure accompanied by abnormal AMR routing or inability to support the affected workflow.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to confirm with the site whether the affected zone is currently unable to get a pair, whether AMRs are routing to the hospital lane instead of the expected workflow, whether a low-battery or physically obstructed AMR is involved, and whether RMS shows the same abnormal fleet or pairing presentation; use generic affected-zone and reported-robot references rather than incident-specific identifiers.
nodes.source_supported_description: The site reported inability to get a pair, AMRs going to the hospital, and an earlier low-battery AMR condition. RMS artifacts show status tables with abnormal-looking red entries, but exact values are unreadable.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to confirm with the site whether the affected zone is currently unable to get a pair, whether AMRs are routing to the hospital lane instead of the expected workflow, whether a low-battery or physically obstructed AMR is involved, and whether RMS shows the same abnormal fleet or pairing presentation; use generic affected-zone and reported-robot references rather than incident-specific identifiers.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site or L1 support observes the affected zone behavior through site interview and, when available, the RMS fleet or status view. Healthy or alternate signal: the zone can obtain a pair and AMRs route to the expected workflow. Unhealthy signal: the zone cannot obtain a pair, AMRs consistently route to the hospital, or the site reports an AMR unable to support the workflow. Inconclusive: the report is intermittent, the affected workflow cannot be reproduced, or the RMS view is unavailable or unreadable.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: Support messages record direct phone discussion with the site about inability to get a pair, low battery, replacement AMRs, and hospital routing; source refs case_228723:page_1 and case_228723:page_2.
The page 6 artifact is visibly an RMS web UI with robot or system status tables and red-highlighted entries; source ref case_228723:page_6.

relevant_evidence: The source discusses AMR add/remove handling, possible roster problems, and abnormal RMS status.

ontology_gaps: The supplied ontology snippet does not establish a specific backend mapping for zone pairing state or hospital-lane routing for this node.
healthy_indicators: Site reports that the affected zone can obtain a pair.
AMRs are observed supporting the expected workflow rather than uniformly routing to the hospital.
RMS presents a consistent normal fleet state without the reported abnormal entries.
unhealthy_indicators: Site reports that the affected zone cannot obtain a pair.
Multiple or replacement AMRs route to the hospital lane.
A low-battery or physically constrained AMR is reported in the affected area.
RMS shows exception-style or red-highlighted robot status entries.
inconclusive_indicators: The site cannot reproduce the pairing failure.
Only one ambiguous AMR symptom is reported without confirming zone impact.
RMS is unavailable or the relevant table details cannot be read.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Site reports under zone 5, they're unable to get a pair.
Earlier low-battery AMR issues and replacement AMRs going to the hospital lane.
RMS web UI with robot or system status tables and multiple red-highlighted entries; exact values are unreadable.

nodes.primary_action: Confirm the reported pairing failure and abnormal AMR routing status (including whether any low-battery or physically constrained AMR is currently involved) by gathering both site interview observations and a readable RMS pairing/fleet-status view if available.
evidence_to_collect: Site confirmation of: zone can vs cannot obtain a pair (and whether the symptom is currently present or intermittent).
Site confirmation of AMR routing behavior: expected workflow vs consistently routing to the hospital lane.
Site description of any low-battery / physically obstructed AMR under racks (as a suspected current condition, not assumed root cause).
RMS evidence (when available and readable): fleet/robot/status presentation that matches the symptom (pairing failure and/or abnormal entries) vs a normal state.
nodes.healthy_interpretation: The affected zone can obtain a pair and AMRs support the expected workflow rather than uniformly routing to the hospital; any RMS presentation is consistent with normal fleet state (no abnormal/red-highlight indicators that correlate to the report).
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: The affected zone cannot obtain a pair, AMRs consistently route to the hospital lane, and/or site reports an AMR unable to support the workflow; RMS shows corresponding abnormal/exception-style entries (even if exact values are initially unclear).
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: The report is intermittent/not reproducible, RMS is unavailable/unreadable for the relevant status table, or the evidence is insufficient to link the AMR routing/pairing symptom to current fleet state.
nodes.generated_guidance: Treat the symptoms as a current-state confirmation task. Do not assume low battery is the root cause; only confirm it as a suspected current condition. Prefer to obtain a readable RMS view that correlates with the reported pairing/routing behavior; if RMS values cannot be read, escalate via the evidence ambiguity gate rather than inferring the roster/mapping fault.

nodes.title: Determine whether AMR roster or mapping state is abnormal
nodes.intent: Determine whether recent AMR replacement or remove/add activity left an AMR missing, unmapped, incorrectly rostered, or otherwise unable to receive the expected task.
nodes.goal: Determine whether recent AMR replacement or remove/add activity left an AMR missing, unmapped, incorrectly rostered, or otherwise unable to receive the expected task.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to inspect the RMS fleet or robot status view for the affected AMR's roster membership, mapped or unmapped indication, location, and assignment-related abnormal state, and to compare the displayed state with the site's reported remove/add history without relying on incident-specific robot identifiers.
nodes.source_supported_description: Support discussion proposed improper remove/add or RMS rostering as a possible explanation. Resolution text states that a robot was shown as not mapped, but the source does not prove that this was the confirmed root cause.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to inspect the RMS fleet or robot status view for the affected AMR's roster membership, mapped or unmapped indication, location, and assignment-related abnormal state, and to compare the displayed state with the site's reported remove/add history without relying on incident-specific robot identifiers.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site or L1 support observes the RMS roster or robot status view. Healthy signal: affected AMRs appear as expected members of the fleet with consistent mapped or assigned state and no relevant exception indication. Unhealthy signal: an AMR is absent, shown as not mapped, has an abnormal roster state, or does not receive the expected task after replacement or remove/add activity. Inconclusive: the RMS view is too unclear to identify the relevant state, or the site history does not establish which AMR was replaced or added.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: Support discussion explicitly refers to robots being properly rostered in RMS, and the artifact shows RMS status tables; source refs case_228723:page_2, case_228723:page_5, and case_228723:page_6.

relevant_evidence: The source explicitly raises improper remove/add handling, RMS rostering, and a robot shown as not mapped.

ontology_gaps: The supplied ontology snippet does not provide a specific backend field mapping for task assignment eligibility or zone pairing correlation.
healthy_indicators: The relevant AMR is present in the expected RMS roster.
The AMR is shown with a normal mapped or assigned state.
The AMR's displayed location and assignment state are consistent with the site's reported physical state.
unhealthy_indicators: The AMR is shown as not mapped or otherwise absent from the expected roster.
The displayed roster or mapping state conflicts with the physical or site-reported state.
The AMR remains unable to receive the expected task after replacement or add activity.
inconclusive_indicators: The RMS screenshot does not expose readable identifiers or status meanings.
The site cannot identify the affected AMR or the sequence of replacement activity.
The displayed state is abnormal but cannot be linked to the pairing symptom.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Support suggested robots may not have been removed and added properly and referred to RMS rostering.
RMS status tables with red-highlighted entries; exact status values are not readable.
Resolution details state that a removed robot was shown as not mapped.

nodes.primary_action: Inspect RMS roster/map state for the fleet/robots associated with the symptom to determine whether a specific AMR is missing, unmapped/not mapped, incorrectly rostered, or otherwise unable to receive expected tasks—then correlate that abnormal mapping to the site’s remove/add history (without relying on unreadable identifiers).
evidence_to_collect: RMS fleet/robot status evidence showing whether affected AMRs are present in roster vs absent/not mapped.
RMS indications of abnormal roster/mapping/assignment-relevant state that can plausibly explain pairing failure/hospital diversion.
Displayed location and assignment state that can be compared to the site’s physical state/describe of constrained AMR (e.g., under rack/low battery).
Any evidence linking the abnormal mapping state to recent remove/add activity (as described by site).
nodes.healthy_interpretation: The relevant AMRs are present in the expected RMS roster and shown with normal mapped/assigned state; their displayed location/assignment is consistent with site-reported physical state; no unmapped/exception roster/mapping persists that correlates to the symptom.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: An AMR is shown as not mapped/absent or in an abnormal roster/mapping state conflicting with the site’s reported physical state and/or correlating with failure to support tasks after replacement/remove/add.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: The RMS screenshot/view is too unclear to identify relevant roster/mapping state or the site cannot identify which AMR(s) were replaced/added; abnormal presentation cannot be reliably linked to the symptom.

optional_corroboration.note: If RMS roster/mapping evidence is unclear, corroborate using available SSMS/DB evidence on robot location/roster state only when the same fleet-state can be identified; otherwise use the escalation gate.

nodes.generated_guidance: Use RMS to decide if the issue is a roster/mapping problem worth pursuing with an authorized site isolation/remove action. If RMS values are unreadable or you cannot link the abnormal mapping state to the pairing/routing symptom, do not infer—route to the escalation gate (node_6).

nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to apply the decision rubric for an AMR shown as unmapped or incorrectly rostered, including comparison of RMS state with site physical confirmation and the safety and authorization criteria for any site-side isolation or remove-from-system action; do not encode exact remove/add steps here.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source records site-side removal of a robot from the system and placement on charger after discussion of roster and mapping concerns. It does not provide a complete or repeatable removal/add procedure.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to apply the decision rubric for an AMR shown as unmapped or incorrectly rostered, including comparison of RMS state with site physical confirmation and the safety and authorization criteria for any site-side isolation or remove-from-system action; do not encode exact remove/add steps here.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site or L1 support compares the RMS roster or mapping indication with the physical and reported AMR state. Recovery-path signal: a specific AMR is shown or reported as unmapped, incorrectly rostered, or otherwise associated with the pairing failure, and an authorized site role can safely isolate it. Alternate signal: the roster or mapping state appears normal, the issue is not linked to one AMR, or the site cannot safely perform the supported action. Inconclusive: the evidence is contradictory or the relevant RMS state cannot be established.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: RMS screenshots and support discussion were used to consider roster and mapping state; source refs case_228723:page_2 and case_228723:page_6.

relevant_evidence: The source describes a suspected roster or mapping problem and a site-side robot removal action.
The source reports an AMR under a rack, an AMR placed on charger, and removal from the system.

ontology_gaps: The supplied ontology does not define a specific authorization or safety rubric for this remove-from-system decision.
The source does not establish whether a system-side remove/add operation or only physical isolation was performed.
healthy_indicators: RMS and site confirmation show normal roster or mapping state.
No specific AMR can be linked to the pairing failure.
The site cannot safely or permissibly perform the potential isolation action.
unhealthy_indicators: RMS indicates an unmapped or abnormal roster state associated with the affected workflow.
The site confirms the same AMR is physically constrained, unavailable, or placed out of service.
The remove-from-system path is authorized and supported by the available evidence.
inconclusive_indicators: RMS and physical observations disagree.
The source does not identify whether the displayed abnormal state is current.
Safety, authorization, or physical access prerequisites are not confirmed.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: Do not direct an unauthorized role to perform fleet-control or physical recovery actions. If the evidence does not establish a safe supported path, use the escalation gate.

nodes.primary_action: Use the evidence to choose whether an authorized site role should proceed with isolation/remove-from-system of the identified unmapped/incorrectly rostered AMR, or whether the evidence does not support that recovery path (or is unsafe/unauthorized).
evidence_to_collect: RMS roster/mapping evidence showing the AMR that is believed to be unmapped/incorrectly rostered and associated with the symptom.
Site physical confirmation that the AMR is the one to isolate (e.g., the robot described by the site is constrained/under rack/low battery or placed on charger per the incident history).
Safety/authorization prerequisites are satisfied for the isolate/remove action (confirm role limits and that an allowed charging/holding state can be used).
Whether site can safely and authoritatively perform the supported action under approved procedure boundaries.
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Evidence shows a specific AMR associated with symptom that can be safely isolated/removed, and authorization/safety prerequisites are met by the site and supported by available evidence.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: RMS indicates unmapped/abnormal roster state and site confirms the same AMR is physically constrained/unavailable/out of service, and the remove/isolation path is authorized and supported by evidence.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: RMS and physical observations disagree, current abnormal state can’t be confirmed as current, or authorization/safety prerequisites are not confirmed.

optional_corroboration.note: If the AMR selection cannot be confidently linked between RMS roster state and physical robot identity, do not proceed with isolation—use escalation (node_6).

linked_primary_procedure.link_rationale: Node_3 is a branching decision, not the recovery execution itself. A recovery procedure must be linked at node_4 when proceeding to the authorized isolation/remove action.
match_gaps: No explicit diagnostic decision rubric procedure (in candidates) suitable for step-level branching; recovery is handled in node_4.

nodes.generated_guidance: Only proceed to the recovery action if both (1) RMS supports an unmapped/incorrectly rostered AMR linked to the symptom and (2) the site can safely isolate/remove it under an approved, role-limited procedure and place it in an appropriate safe charging/holding state.

nodes.title: Perform authorized AMR isolation or removal action
nodes.intent: Carry out the source-supported high-level recovery action when the affected AMR is linked to the abnormal roster or mapping state and the authorized site procedure permits it.
nodes.goal: Carry out the source-supported high-level recovery action when the affected AMR is linked to the abnormal roster or mapping state and the authorized site procedure permits it.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed for authorized site-side AMR isolation or removal from active system participation, including physical safety prerequisites, charging or holding-state requirements, RMS state confirmation, and role limits; the procedure must define the approved remove/add handling without embedding exact operational steps here.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source-supported recovery was site removal of an AMR from the system followed by placement on charger. The source does not document exact steps and does not establish that this action is universally appropriate.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed for authorized site-side AMR isolation or removal from active system participation, including physical safety prerequisites, charging or holding-state requirements, RMS state confirmation, and role limits; the procedure must define the approved remove/add handling without embedding exact operational steps here.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The authorized site role observes that the affected AMR has been removed from active system participation and placed in a safe charging or holding state, consistent with the source-reported recovery action. Progress signal: the AMR is no longer contributing to the abnormal pairing behavior. Unsuccessful signal: the AMR remains active in the problematic state or the site cannot complete the authorized action. Inconclusive: the action is reported but the resulting RMS or operational state cannot be confirmed.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The source reports removal from the system and includes RMS screenshots showing robot status tables; source refs case_228723:page_6 and case_228723:page_10.

ontology_gaps: The supplied ontology does not provide a complete cataloged procedure for the specific remove-from-system action described in the incident.
healthy_indicators: The authorized site role confirms the affected AMR is isolated from active operation.
The AMR is confirmed in the intended charging or holding state.
RMS no longer presents the AMR as contributing to the abnormal pairing condition.
unhealthy_indicators: The AMR remains active in the problematic fleet state.
The site cannot place the AMR in a safe holding or charging state.
The pairing symptom continues immediately after the authorized action.
inconclusive_indicators: Only the physical action is reported without a corresponding system-state confirmation.
The site cannot confirm which AMR was isolated.
RMS status remains unreadable or contradictory.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: Stop if physical safety, authorization, or approved remove/add prerequisites are not satisfied. Do not substitute this node for the exact site procedure.

nodes.primary_action: Perform an authorized AMR isolation/remove-from-active-system action for the identified unmapped/incorrectly rostered AMR and place it into the safe charging/holding state, then confirm it is no longer contributing to abnormal pairing/hospital-routing behavior.
evidence_to_collect: Before action: RMS confirms the target AMR’s abnormal/unmapped state that is linked to the symptom.
During/after action: site confirms the AMR is removed from active system participation and placed into safe charging/holding state.
After action: RMS no longer presents that AMR as contributing to the abnormal pairing behavior (or symptom correlation improves).
Whether site can complete the authorized action successfully without leaving the AMR active in the problematic state.
nodes.healthy_interpretation: The AMR is isolated/removed from active operation and placed in the intended safe charging/holding state; RMS no longer shows it as contributing to the abnormal pairing condition.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: The AMR remains active in the problematic fleet state after the site action, or the AMR cannot be placed into a safe holding/charging state; symptom persists immediately after action.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Only the physical action is reported without corresponding system-state confirmation, or RMS evidence is unreadable/unavailable or contradictory.

optional_corroboration.note: After physical isolation, use RMS read-only status to verify the AMR is no longer associated with the abnormal mapping/pair-fail presentation.

nodes.generated_guidance: Use only an approved, role-limited remove/isolate procedure appropriate to the evidence (unmapped/roster-mapping issue leading to pairing failure). Do not attempt additional recovery steps beyond what the authorized procedure covers.

ontology_evidence.concept_evidence: Isolation/remove-from-active operation is appropriate only after mapping/roster mismatch evidence is established; safe charging/holding is required by the incident pattern.

nodes.diagnostic_interpretation: Execute the authorized high-level recovery action and gather confirmatory system-state evidence so node_5 validation can be performed.

nodes.trigger_condition: The authorized site role observes that the affected AMR has been removed from active system participation and placed in a safe charging or holding state, consistent with the source-reported recovery action. nodes.title: Validate restored pairing and stable AMR operation
nodes.intent: Confirm that the affected workflow has recovered after the authorized fleet-state action and remains operational during observation.
nodes.goal: Confirm that the affected workflow has recovered after the authorized fleet-state action and remains operational during observation.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to validate the affected zone's pairing behavior through site observation, confirm expected AMR routing and fleet state in RMS, and define a short stability-monitoring period before declaring recovery; include criteria for failed validation and evidence capture without prescribing exact screen navigation.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source reports that operation resumed after robot removal and remained operational during approximately 10 minutes of monitoring, while acknowledging that the recovery was reported rather than independently confirmed by readable live RMS details.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to validate the affected zone's pairing behavior through site observation, confirm expected AMR routing and fleet state in RMS, and define a short stability-monitoring period before declaring recovery; include criteria for failed validation and evidence capture without prescribing exact screen navigation.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site observes the affected workflow and, when available, checks RMS status. Healthy signal: the zone can obtain a pair, AMRs resume expected operation rather than uniformly routing to the hospital, and the system remains operational during a short monitoring period. Unhealthy signal: pairing remains unavailable, AMRs continue abnormal hospital routing, or the same roster or mapping symptom returns. Inconclusive: recovery is reported but no direct operational observation or readable RMS confirmation is available.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The source reports that the site believed the system had begun working and that support remained on the call to monitor operation; source refs case_228723:page_7 and case_228723:page_10.
The page 10 artifact contains embedded RMS screenshots associated with the reported recovery, although detailed status values are not readable; source ref case_228723:page_10.

relevant_evidence: The source uses RMS screenshots and reports continued operation after removal of the affected AMR.

ontology_gaps: The supplied ontology snippet does not establish a specific backend validation mapping for pair acquisition or hospital-lane routing.
healthy_indicators: The site confirms that the affected zone can obtain a pair.
AMRs resume the expected workflow instead of consistently routing to the hospital.
The system remains operational during the reported short monitoring period.
RMS no longer shows the relevant abnormal roster or mapping indication.
unhealthy_indicators: The zone remains unable to get a pair.
AMRs continue routing abnormally to the hospital.
The same or another fleet-state anomaly reappears during monitoring.
The reported recovery cannot be reproduced by the site.
inconclusive_indicators: Recovery is based only on a case note or message without direct site observation.
The monitoring period is too short to assess stability.
RMS screenshots or status views are unavailable or unreadable.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: If pairing or normal AMR routing does not recover, or if the abnormal state returns during monitoring, stop this path and use the escalation gate.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Site believed removing the robot may have fixed the issue and reported that the system had begun working.
System reportedly began functioning again and remained operational during approximately 10 minutes of monitoring.

nodes.primary_action: Validate that the affected workflow returns to normal operation after the authorized fleet-state action, by confirming zone pairing success and expected AMR routing behavior, and monitoring stability briefly before declaring recovery.
nodes.primary_surface: site observation + RMS UI (read-only when available)
evidence_to_collect: Site observation that the affected zone can obtain a pair after the action.
Site observation that AMRs resume expected operation (not consistently routing to hospital lane).
RMS read-only confirmation that the abnormal roster/mapping symptom is no longer present or is reduced in correlation with the zone pairing.
Monitoring evidence during a short stability window (reported ~10 minutes in the incident) showing continued operation and absence of re-diversion/re-pair failure.
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Zone pairing succeeds; AMRs resume expected operation; the system remains operational during the monitoring window; RMS no longer shows the relevant abnormal roster/mapping indication (when readable).
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Zone pairing remains unavailable; AMRs continue abnormal hospital routing; the same fleet-state symptom returns during monitoring; recovery cannot be reproduced by the site.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Recovery is based only on messages/case notes without direct site observation; monitoring window is insufficient; RMS evidence is unavailable/unreadable.

optional_corroboration.note: If RMS screenshots are unreadable, prioritize site-observed pairing + routing confirmation and capture a new readable RMS snapshot for correlation.

nodes.generated_guidance: Do not declare recovery solely because the site reports success; ensure at least site-level pairing + routing behavior is confirmed and stability is observed briefly. If pairing remains unavailable or diversion returns, route to the escalation gate (node_6).

nodes.title: Stop if the supported fleet-state path does not restore operation
nodes.intent: Stop and hand off when the roster or mapping evidence is inconclusive, the authorized recovery action cannot be performed safely, or validation fails after the supported path.
nodes.goal: Stop and hand off when the roster or mapping evidence is inconclusive, the authorized recovery action cannot be performed safely, or validation fails after the supported path.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to prepare a technical escalation handoff with the site symptom description, RMS roster or mapping evidence, physical AMR state, remove/add or isolation actions attempted, pairing and hospital-routing observations, monitoring results, and explicit stop or safety conditions.
nodes.source_supported_description: The incident contains ambiguous RMS evidence, unresolved symptoms after an earlier remove/add attempt, and reported recovery that required monitoring. These support a stop condition when the lightweight path cannot establish or restore the expected state.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to prepare a technical escalation handoff with the site symptom description, RMS roster or mapping evidence, physical AMR state, remove/add or isolation actions attempted, pairing and hospital-routing observations, monitoring results, and explicit stop or safety conditions.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: L1 or L2 support observes one of the following: the affected AMR state cannot be established in RMS, site safety or authorization prerequisites are absent, the AMR cannot be isolated under the approved procedure, pairing remains unavailable, or abnormal hospital routing continues after recovery. Healthy exit for this gate is not applicable; the gate is entered only when the troubleshooting path cannot continue safely or has not restored operation.

nodes.primary_action: Stop the unsupported path and prepare a technical escalation handoff to L2/L3 with the symptom description, evidence package (RMS roster/mapping evidence as available), physical AMR state, actions attempted, pairing/hospital-routing observations, and monitoring results plus explicit stop/safety conditions.
evidence_to_collect: Symptom statement: zone pairing failure and abnormal AMR routing/hospital diversion (as reported).
RMS evidence: roster/mapping state screenshots or notes (including the fact that values may be unreadable/ambiguous).
Physical AMR state as confirmed by site (e.g., low battery/under rack; whether AMR was removed/placed on charger).
Actions attempted under supported/authorized path: remove/add/isolation attempt (high-level only), and whether completed safely.
Validation/monitoring results: whether pairing/routing recovered and whether it stayed stable during observation; any reappearance.
Explicit stop conditions met: inability to establish current RMS state, unreadable/contradictory evidence, inability to safely perform authorized recovery, or validation failure after recovery.
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Not applicable as a continuing-path gate; the gate is entered when troubleshooting cannot safely continue or has not restored operation.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Evidence indicates unresolved symptoms (pair fail persists; abnormal hospital routing persists; mapping state unexplained) or site cannot safely perform/complete the authorized action.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: RMS details are unreadable or evidence contradicts; recovery is reported but cannot be reproduced/monitored reliably.
nodes.generated_guidance: Do not infer roster/mapping faults from ambiguous/unreadable RMS screenshots or from narrative-only recovery. Compile what is known, explicitly mark missing evidence, and hand off for deeper investigation/ownership beyond this candidate playbook.

ontology_evidence.concept_evidence: Gate is consistent with escalation when roster/mapping evidence cannot be established or linked to symptoms.

nodes.diagnostic_interpretation: Stop and escalate when evidence ambiguity/safety/authorization gaps or validation failures prevent continuing the supported recovery path.

evidence_to_collect: Site observation: bag-out stopped vs partially progressing vs normal automated progression

nodes.healthy_interpretation: Bag-out progresses normally with active AGV movement/routing; manual bagging is not required.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Bag-out is stopped or only partially progressing and/or requires manual bagging; site reports prolonged AGV inactivity and/or out-of-sequence/pairing/tote/HMI symptoms.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Bag-out state cannot be clearly observed by the site, the affected area/robot behavior cannot be identified in RMS, or the relevant HMI/operational state is unavailable/readable.

optional_corroboration.note: If the site reports prolonged AGV inactivity, corroborate that the problem is tied to active AGV/system faults using an AGV active-error evidence path (RMS overview, then SSMS/WCS read-only if needed).

nodes.generated_guidance: Use the site’s bag-out observation to determine whether you are dealing with a true stoppage vs partial progression, and gather which categories of symptoms are present (AGV movement, sequence/pair exchange, tote/task state, hospital HMI fault). Treat any sequence/pair/tote/HMI observations as hypotheses until you corroborate them with RMS/active-error evidence.

nodes.title: Determine whether an AGV active error or abnormal fleet state is present
nodes.intent: Determine whether an AGV, robot, or system active-error condition correlates with the bag-out stoppage.
nodes.goal: Determine whether an AGV, robot, or system active-error condition correlates with the bag-out stoppage.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to inspect the RMS fleet and activity views for active AGV faults, prolonged inactivity, unavailable robots, and abnormal status associated with the affected bag-out flow, and to review the source-named system active-error view when available. The procedure should define how to interpret an active error versus an unavailable or merely idle robot without prescribing commands.
nodes.source_supported_description: Support reported checking activity and finding an AGV that had not moved for three hours, while the discussion also referred to checking system active error because the Aveva screen was not visible.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to inspect the RMS fleet and activity views for active AGV faults, prolonged inactivity, unavailable robots, and abnormal status associated with the affected bag-out flow, and to review the source-named system active-error view when available. The procedure should define how to interpret an active error versus an unavailable or merely idle robot without prescribing commands.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The operator or L1 support reviews RMS fleet/activity status and, where available to the support role, the system active-error view. Unhealthy signals are an active AGV fault, prolonged inactivity, or an abnormal robot status associated with the stalled workflow. Healthy signal is no active error and expected movement or availability. Inconclusive means the active-error view is unavailable, the robot cannot be identified, or the evidence does not correlate with the stoppage.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The page 11 artifact is an RMS-style screenshot showing an AGV that did not move for three hours.
The incident discussion says the screen could not be seen in Aveva and suggested checking system active error.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The source explicitly references checking system active error and provides RMS evidence of prolonged AGV inactivity.

ontology_gaps: The supplied ontology snippet does not establish a validated backend mapping for the source-named system active-error view.
healthy_indicators: No relevant active AGV error is displayed.
The affected AGV or pair shows expected activity and availability.
unhealthy_indicators: An active AGV or system error is displayed.
The affected AGV remains inactive or unavailable.
The fleet view indicates a robot state inconsistent with the bag-out workflow.
inconclusive_indicators: The Aveva or system active-error screen cannot be viewed.
RMS activity data is stale or the affected AGV cannot be identified.
The displayed error cannot be correlated to the bag-out symptom.

nodes.primary_action: Determine whether an active AGV/system error or abnormal fleet/robot state is present that correlates with the bag-out stoppage by reviewing RMS fleet/activity status and (when the system is viewable to the support role) confirming active-error evidence.
nodes.primary_surface: RMS overall / AGV activity + active-error evidence path (preferred: rms_ui; when viewable: system active-error via supported read-only evidence)
evidence_to_collect: RMS fleet/activity status indicators for prolonged inactivity, alarms/faults, and robot state inconsistent with bag-out expectations
If available: system active-error view evidence (error presence/absence) to differentiate active fault vs idle/unavailable
Correlation notes: whether the time window and the affected behavior match the bag-out stoppage
nodes.healthy_interpretation: No relevant active AGV/system error is displayed and the affected AGV/pair shows expected movement/availability consistent with bag-out progression.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: An active AGV/system error is displayed and the affected AGV remains inactive/unavailable; fleet view shows robot state inconsistent with the stalled workflow.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: The active-error view is unavailable/unreadable, RMS activity is stale/unidentifiable, or errors cannot be correlated to the bag-out symptom.

optional_corroboration.note: If Aveva/system active-error evidence cannot be viewed or correlated, avoid assuming cause from RMS inactivity alone; proceed using hospital HMI/tote/task evidence branch or escalate when evidence remains unattainable.

linked_primary_procedure.title: Check Overall System Faults and Active AGV Faults on the Overall System RMS Page
linked_primary_procedure.purpose: Open an RMS overall page and identify whether there are active system faults/active AGV faults relevant to the observed bag-out stoppage.
linked_primary_procedure.rationale: Strong match to node intent: determine active AGV/system fault state and correlate to bag-out stoppage; retrieval score is highest among node_2 candidates and aligns to the RMS evidence path described in the case.
match_gaps: Node_2 also mentions checking a source-named system active-error view (Aveva/system active-error). This candidate is RMS-focused; it may not cover the Aveva/system active-error screen correlation.

nodes.generated_guidance: First, use RMS overall/AGV fault indicators to decide whether the system is healthy vs faulted. If active-error evidence exists, treat it as causal until you validate correlation with the bag-out symptom. If no active error exists (or active-error view is unreadable), keep hospital HMI/tote/task hypotheses as unconfirmed and branch to sequence/pair/tote/task discrimination.

nodes.intent: Distinguish an AGV sequence or pairing concern from a tote or task condition visible through the hospital-area HMI.
nodes.goal: Distinguish an AGV sequence or pairing concern from a tote or task condition visible through the hospital-area HMI.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Decision-rubric procedure needed to compare the site-reported sequence or pairing concern with the hospital HMI's visible fault or task state, the tote identity and physical location, and the RMS activity observation. The procedure should define when a reported HMI fault or tote mismatch is relevant to bag-out and when it should be treated as unconfirmed.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source reports a tote read at the hospital while physically elsewhere, a hospital HMI fault, a stuck task visible only on that HMI, and a suspected robot out-of-sequence condition. These remain source-supported observations and hypotheses rather than confirmed cause.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Decision-rubric procedure needed to compare the site-reported sequence or pairing concern with the hospital HMI's visible fault or task state, the tote identity and physical location, and the RMS activity observation. The procedure should define when a reported HMI fault or tote mismatch is relevant to bag-out and when it should be treated as unconfirmed.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site/operator checks the relevant hospital HMI and reports whether it shows a fault, a stuck task, or a tote identity/state inconsistent with the physical workflow; support correlates that report with RMS activity and the bag-out symptom. Unhealthy-style signals are a reported stuck task, HMI fault, or tote read in an unexpected location. Healthy-style signal is no such condition and the robot or pair is operating normally. Inconclusive means the HMI is unavailable, the fault text is unreadable, or the tote/task relationship cannot be confirmed.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The page 12 artifact is an HMI-like screen and the surrounding message states that the hospital HMI was showing a fault.
The page 11 artifact is an RMS-style activity screenshot showing prolonged AGV inactivity.
The site reported that a tote was read at the hospital while physically elsewhere and later identified a tote at the hospital during troubleshooting.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: RMS activity and system active-error evidence are the supplied validated diagnostic context for correlating robot state with the workflow stoppage.

ontology_gaps: The supplied ontology snippets do not provide a validated capability mapping for hospital-HMI stuck-task or tote-location interpretation.
healthy_indicators: The hospital HMI shows no relevant fault or stuck task.
The tote identity and physical location agree.
AGV pair and sequence observations are consistent with normal operation.
unhealthy_indicators: The hospital HMI shows a fault or a stuck task.
A tote is reported in a location different from its system reading.
The site reports an AGV pair or robot sequence inconsistent with the workflow.
inconclusive_indicators: The HMI fault text is unreadable or the HMI cannot be viewed.
The tote identity or physical location cannot be confirmed.
The source evidence does not establish whether the condition is causal.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: A tote was reported read at the hospital while physically in another location; bag-out entered request and did not progress.
The HMI at the hospital is showing a fault.
A prior stuck task was reported as visible only on that HMI.

nodes.primary_action: Use the hospital-area HMI (and tote identity/state it reports) to decide whether the bag-out stoppage is consistent with a sequence/pairing concern versus a tote/task condition that is visible through that HMI; treat all such HMI-reported conditions as unconfirmed until corroborated by correlation with the bag-out symptom and RMS activity.
nodes.primary_surface: Hospital HMI (hospital_hmi) corroborated with RMS activity/status (rms_ui)
evidence_to_collect: Hospital HMI fault indication presence/absence and whether a stuck task is shown
Hospital-reported tote identity and its HMI location/state
Whether the tote identity/location on hospital HMI matches physical workflow expectations
Correlation with RMS activity/status: whether the fleet behavior matches the hospital HMI fault/task pattern
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Hospital HMI shows no relevant fault or stuck task; tote identity/location aligns with the workflow; RMS activity/pair/sequence observations are consistent with normal operation.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Hospital HMI shows a fault and/or stuck task, and/or tote identity is reported in an unexpected location; site reports sequence/pair/tote mismatch inconsistent with workflow.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Hospital HMI cannot be viewed/read; fault text is unreadable; tote/task relationship cannot be confirmed; evidence cannot be tied to the bag-out symptom.

optional_corroboration.note: If hospital HMI indicates a fault/stuck task but correlation is ambiguous, prefer corroborating with RMS fleet activity/state before taking any state-changing recovery action.

linked_primary_procedure.title: Check Hospital HMI Operations Screen Induct/Extract Position Read-Only Data and WCS Status Messages
linked_primary_procedure.purpose: Review hospital HMI read-only position/induct-extract information and any related status messages that help determine whether a hospital-area fault/stuck-task condition is present for the bag-out flow.
linked_primary_procedure.rationale: Best matching candidate for the node’s explicit requirement to inspect hospital HMI evidence (fault/task) while keeping it read-only/interpretive; aligns to node_3 intent and has strong combined score among candidates for this node type.
match_gaps: Node_3 also needs decision rubric logic comparing sequence/pairing concern vs tote/task condition; this candidate supports hospital evidence review but does not encode the full rubric.

nodes.generated_guidance: Decide whether the hospital HMI evidence points to: (A) a stuck task/fault that can block the bag-out exchange flow, or (B) a sequence/pairing issue manifested as an apparent mismatch between what the hospital HMI is showing and what RMS activity indicates. If HMI evidence is unreadable/unavailable, treat as inconclusive and hand off for escalation/evidence gathering rather than guessing recovery actions.

nodes.source_supported_description: The incident records robots being turned off because of low batteries, later turned back on, AGV pairs being removed and added, and advice to acknowledge and retry an HMI fault. The source does not isolate which action produced the final recovery.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed for the authorized recovery path selected from the diagnostic evidence, including applicable AGV pair remove/add or replacement handling, robot availability and battery prerequisites, hospital HMI fault acknowledgement or retry when authorized, and any approved stuck-task recovery boundaries. The procedure must define role limits and must not assume that a specific robot or root cause has been confirmed.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The authorized site or support role completes the applicable recovery procedure. A recovery-progress signal is that affected robots remain powered and available, the relevant pair or sequence is restored, or the identified task/tote condition is cleared. An unhealthy signal is that the same AGV or task remains unavailable or bag-out stops again. Inconclusive means the source-supported recovery option is not authorized, the condition cannot be identified, or the procedure outcome cannot be observed.
