nodes.title: Validate restored sequence and sustained bag-out operation
nodes.intent: Confirm that robots are functional, the relevant sequence is stable, and bag-out completes or continues normally without immediate recurrence.
nodes.goal: Confirm that robots are functional, the relevant sequence is stable, and bag-out completes or continues normally without immediate recurrence.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to validate the recovered workflow by observing bag-out progress, confirming robot movement and sequence through the RMS activity/status view when available, checking that any relevant HMI fault or task indication is cleared, and obtaining site confirmation that automated operation remains functional before declaring recovery.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source states that with all robots in proper sequence the customer confirmed they were functional. It also records a temporary bag-out restart followed by another stop, so sustained validation is necessary.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to validate the recovered workflow by observing bag-out progress, confirming robot movement and sequence through the RMS activity/status view when available, checking that any relevant HMI fault or task indication is cleared, and obtaining site confirmation that automated operation remains functional before declaring recovery.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site/operator observes the bag-out workflow and confirms that robots are functional and remain in proper sequence; RMS activity, when available, shows expected movement. Healthy signals are automated bag-out progress, stable robot availability, and customer confirmation that operation is functional. Unhealthy signals are another stoppage, renewed prolonged inactivity, unresolved HMI fault, or a task that remains stuck. Inconclusive means only a temporary improvement is observed or the site cannot monitor the next workflow phase.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The incident includes an RMS-style activity screenshot used to observe AGV movement.
The incident includes an HMI artifact and reports that the tote/HMI condition was good after the troubleshooting exchange.
The customer confirmed that the robots were functional when all robots were in proper sequence.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: RMS activity and active-error observations are the source-supported means of corroborating that the AGV abnormal state has cleared.

ontology_gaps: The supplied ontology does not establish a validated mapping for complete bag-out or hospital-HMI task validation.
healthy_indicators: The site confirms robots are functional.
Robots remain in proper sequence and show expected activity.
Bag-out proceeds without returning to manual handling.
The relevant HMI fault or stuck-task indication is no longer present.
unhealthy_indicators: Bag-out stops again or remains incomplete.
An AGV again shows prolonged inactivity or an active error.
The HMI fault or stuck task persists.
The site cannot confirm functional automated operation.
inconclusive_indicators: Only a short period of robot uptime is observed.
Bag-out has not reached the relevant validation point.
RMS or HMI evidence is unavailable or unreadable.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: With all the robots in proper sequence the customer confirms that they are functional.
Bag-out started, processed most items, but stopped again.
The tote at the hospital was identified and the site reported that all was good.

nodes.primary_action: Validate that recovery is sustained: confirm robots remain functional and in proper sequence, bag-out completes or continues normally without immediate recurrence, and any hospital HMI fault/task indication is cleared.
nodes.primary_surface: RMS activity/status (rms_ui) and hospital HMI (hospital_hmi) with site confirmation
evidence_to_collect: Site confirmation that robots are functional and remain in proper sequence
RMS activity/status evidence showing expected robot movement/activity consistent with bag-out continuation (when available)
Hospital HMI fault/stuck-task indication is cleared or no longer present
Bag-out behavior over the next phase: completes/continues automatically and does not revert to manual bagging
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Automated bag-out progresses and/or completes; robots remain functional and in proper sequence; HMI fault/task indication cleared; no recurrence.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Bag-out stops again or remains incomplete; robots again show prolonged inactivity/active error; hospital HMI fault/task remains present; site cannot confirm sustained automated operation.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Only temporary improvement is seen or bag-out has not reached the relevant validation point; RMS/HMI evidence cannot be observed/read.

optional_corroboration.note: If uncertainty remains, corroborate robot movement/activity with an additional RMS view before deciding whether to escalate.

linked_primary_procedure.title: Verify System Bag Out Behavior (close destinations + exchange totes with parcels)
linked_primary_procedure.purpose: Use an evidence-based check to confirm bag-out behavior proceeds through expected exchange/closeout behavior after recovery.
linked_primary_procedure.rationale: Node_5 is explicitly about sustained bag-out validation. This candidate is the closest match to bag-out behavior validation rather than generic RMS fault checks.
match_gaps: Node_5 also requires sequence stability/robot movement validation; this procedure may not fully cover sequence-specific corroboration.

nodes.generated_guidance: Perform a short monitoring window to verify sustained automated bag-out progress. Do not declare recovery based only on a brief restart; require stable robot availability and no recurrence at the bag-out validation point.

nodes.title: Stop and escalate when the supported path does not restore stable operation
nodes.intent: Hand off when the abnormal state cannot be identified, authorized recovery is unavailable or unsuccessful, or validation fails after the supported troubleshooting path.
nodes.goal: Hand off when the abnormal state cannot be identified, authorized recovery is unavailable or unsuccessful, or validation fails after the supported troubleshooting path.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to prepare an escalation handoff with RMS activity and active-error evidence, HMI fault or stuck-task evidence, bag-out behavior, AGV sequence or pair changes attempted, robot power or availability observations, tote observations, validation results, and the limits or authorization constraints that prevented further action.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source records that available troubleshooting options were exhausted at one point, that a prior pair adjustment only temporarily restored bag-out, and that the HMI/task issue required follow-up.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to prepare an escalation handoff with RMS activity and active-error evidence, HMI fault or stuck-task evidence, bag-out behavior, AGV sequence or pair changes attempted, robot power or availability observations, tote observations, validation results, and the limits or authorization constraints that prevented further action.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: L1 support or the authorized site role determines that diagnostics are unavailable, the condition recurs after recovery, the HMI/task state remains unresolved, or the next action requires a role or procedure not available to the current responder. Healthy outcome for this gate is that escalation is not needed because validation passes. Unhealthy outcome is unresolved or recurring operation. Inconclusive outcome is insufficient evidence to determine whether the system is stable.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The incident includes an RMS-style screenshot showing AGV inactivity.
The incident includes an HMI fault and stuck-task discussion.
The source contains site reports about bag-out, robots, totes, and recovery outcomes.

healthy_indicators: The supported recovery path restores stable automated operation and no handoff is required.
unhealthy_indicators: Bag-out remains stopped or stops again.
The AGV, task, tote, or HMI condition remains unresolved.
Further action requires an unavailable role or unsupported procedure.
inconclusive_indicators: Evidence is insufficient to identify the affected component or validate recovery.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: Escalate for unresolved or unauthorized technical continuation, not merely because the historical incident involved collaboration or a prior case escalation.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: The team reported that available options had been exhausted.
Follow-up was requested for the HMI update and stuck-task recovery process.

nodes.primary_action: Stop and prepare an escalation handoff when the supported diagnostic/recovery path cannot identify the affected component, when authorized recovery cannot be completed or does not restore stable operation, or when validation fails/recurs after recovery attempts.
nodes.primary_surface: Evidence package compilation (RMS activity/fault evidence, hospital HMI fault/stuck-task evidence, tote/task observations, and bag-out behavior)
evidence_to_collect: RMS evidence: AGV inactivity and any active faults observed during node_1/node_2
Hospital HMI evidence: fault indication and/or stuck-task visibility and any tote identity/state observations (or explicit unreadable/ambiguous status)
Bag-out behavior timeline: stopped/partial vs restart attempts and recurrence
What recovery was attempted (category level) and what outcome was observed
Authorization/role limits that prevented further actions
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Validation passes; escalation is not needed because stable automated operation is confirmed.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Bag-out remains stopped/stops again; affected AGV/task/tote/HMI condition remains unresolved; recurrence after attempted supported recovery.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Evidence is insufficient to determine system stability or tie observations to a specific affected component/state.

optional_corroboration.note: If escalation is due to evidence unavailability, document exactly which screens/views were unreadable/unreachable and what fallback evidence was used.

nodes.generated_guidance: Compile an evidence package so the next support tier can own the remaining diagnostics and recovery safely. Include only what is observable/verified from RMS and HMI and note which hypotheses were not corroborated.

ontology_evidence.text_evidence: Escalate patterns when evidence indicates system-level stoppage or diagnostics blocked; roles and surface expectations.

nodes.diagnostic_interpretation: Route to escalation due to unresolved/recurring abnormal state or evidence unavailability.

playbooks.title: Hospital station cannot add or induct totes
playbooks.user_facing_summary: Troubleshoot a hospital-station flow where totes cannot be added or inducted, especially when tote removal still works or an AGV appears in an unexpected location.
playbooks.playbook_goal: Determine whether the hospital induction failure is associated with an abnormal AGV location, roster state, or tote association, then guide authorized recovery and validate that hospital tote add and remove operations work again.
observed_entry_symptoms: The hospital station cannot add or induct totes.
Totes can be removed but cannot be added at the hospital.
A robot or AGV is reported in a shut down state.
An AGV appears not to belong in the displayed location, or two AGVs appear under the same rack or in the same zone.
Hospital backlog or tote flow disruption is reported.
support_user_language_examples: Totes can come out but not go in
Hospital tote add is not working
AGV is in the wrong spot
Two AGVs are under the rack
The hospital station cannot add or induct totes
Totes can be removed but cannot be added at the hospital
A robot or AGV is reported in a shut down state
An AGV appears not to belong in the
Hospital backlog or tote flow disruption is reported
playbooks.confidence_reason: The packet repeatedly documents hospital inability to add or induct totes, AGV location and tote-association anomalies, high-level corrective actions, and successful validation that totes could again be added and removed.

nodes.title: Confirm the hospital induction symptom and current AGV/tote context
nodes.intent: Confirm whether the reported failure is specifically inability to add or induct totes at the hospital station and whether an affected AGV, rack position, or associated tote appears abnormal.
nodes.goal: Confirm whether the reported failure is specifically inability to add or induct totes at the hospital station and whether an affected AGV, rack position, or associated tote appears abnormal.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to interview the site about whether the affected hospital station can add and remove totes, inspect the Hospital HMI or other source-evidenced hospital layout view for the affected station, and compare the displayed AGV placement and tote association with the operator's physical observation.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source reports that the site could remove totes but could not add them, and shows an annotated HMI-style layout in a discussion of an AGV being in the wrong location.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to interview the site about whether the affected hospital station can add and remove totes, inspect the Hospital HMI or other source-evidenced hospital layout view for the affected station, and compare the displayed AGV placement and tote association with the operator's physical observation.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site operator observes the hospital station and reports whether tote removal works while tote addition fails; the operator or L1 support checks the hospital HMI or readable layout view for the affected station and reports whether an AGV is shown in an unexpected location or whether multiple AGVs appear associated with one rack or zone. Healthy signal: tote add and remove both work and no abnormal AGV or tote association is reported. Unhealthy signal: tote add or induction fails, especially with an unexpected AGV or associated tote. Inconclusive: the site cannot reproduce the symptom or the displayed location/association is unreadable.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: Page 8 contains an HMI-style rack/layout screenshot used while discussing hospital tote-add failure and AGV placement.
Teams messages report what the site could and could not do with hospital totes and describe AGV placement.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The packet documents a hospital-area failure with an AGV reported in an unexpected location and multiple AGVs under one rack or in one zone; the capability is relevant as a possible state check, not a confirmed classification.

healthy_indicators: Site reports both adding and removing totes work at the hospital.

unhealthy_indicators: Site reports totes can be removed but not added.

inconclusive_indicators: The symptom is no longer reproducible.

The operator and displayed state disagree without enough evidence to reconcile them.

nodes.primary_action: Interview the site/operator about whether hospital tote removal works while tote add/induct fails, then verify on the hospital HMI whether the affected station shows any unexpected AGV/rack/zone occupancy pattern.
evidence_to_collect: Site report: tote add/induct works or fails at the affected hospital station; tote removal works or fails
Hospital HMI evidence for the affected hospital station: displayed AGV/rack/zone occupancy and any unexpected association pattern
Operator physical observation summary, limited to what can be directly observed at the station (no system changes)
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Hospital tote add/induct works at the affected station and hospital HMI shows no unexpected AGV occupancy or duplicate rack/zone association.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Hospital tote add/induct remains unavailable (especially while removal works) and hospital HMI shows an unexpected AGV/rack/zone occupancy pattern or duplicate occupancy.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: The site cannot reproduce the symptom, or station/HMI labels/identifiers are unreadable, or operator and displayed state cannot be reconciled with available evidence.
nodes.generated_guidance: Treat the induction failure as hospital-station scoped first. Capture (1) the add-vs-remove asymmetry from the site, and (2) whether the hospital HMI shows an AGV/rack/zone occupancy anomaly that could plausibly block induction.

nodes.title: Determine whether AGV and tote state is inconsistent
nodes.intent: Determine whether an AGV removal, unexpected location, duplicate rack occupancy, or disconnected tote association is present and plausibly connected to the hospital induction symptom.
nodes.goal: Determine whether an AGV removal, unexpected location, duplicate rack occupancy, or disconnected tote association is present and plausibly connected to the hospital induction symptom.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to inspect the hospital rack or AGV layout view and, where authorized, the API dog or Aveva-fed AGV and tote state for unexpected AGV placement, duplicate location occupancy, removed-AGV residue, or disconnected tote association; the procedure should define how to record evidence without changing state.
nodes.source_supported_description: The packet repeatedly discusses an AGV in the wrong location, multiple AGVs under a rack, a disconnected tote, and use of API dog or Aveva to correct AGV and tote state.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to inspect the hospital rack or AGV layout view and, where authorized, the API dog or Aveva-fed AGV and tote state for unexpected AGV placement, duplicate location occupancy, removed-AGV residue, or disconnected tote association; the procedure should define how to record evidence without changing state.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The operator observes the physical or displayed AGV position, while L1/L2 support reviews the source-evidenced AGV/layout or API client context when available. Healthy signal: the expected AGV is associated with the expected station or rack and no disconnected tote is present. Unhealthy signal: an AGV is in an unexpected location, two AGVs are shown under one rack or in one zone, or a tote remains associated with an unavailable or removed AGV. Inconclusive: the source view lacks readable identifiers or the association cannot be confirmed.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: Annotated HMI-style rack/layout screenshot was shared alongside the statement that an AGV did not belong in the location.
The packet states that Aveva was used to remove an AGV from a zone and add a tote to a station.

ontology_gaps: No supplied ontology card establishes the backend model or fields for AGV-to-tote association or hospital-station tote ownership.
healthy_indicators: AGV location and station association agree with the expected layout.
No disconnected or orphaned tote association is observed.
unhealthy_indicators: AGV is displayed in an unexpected location.
Two AGVs appear under one rack or in one zone.
A tote remains associated with a removed or disconnected AGV.
inconclusive_indicators: Only a low-resolution annotated layout is available.
The interface does not expose a readable roster, location, or tote association.
The reported anomaly is based only on second-hand discussion.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Summary describes an AGV with a disconnected tote, removal of an inducted tote through API dog, and removal of additional AGVs to restore flow.
Chat says Aveva hits the same endpoints as API dog and was used to remove an AGV from a zone and add a tote to a station.

nodes.primary_action: Verify whether the hospital AGV roster/location state is inconsistent with the expected rack/zone layout and whether a disconnected/orphaned tote association exists, using hospital HMI for what is visible and authorized backend reads when available.
evidence_to_collect: Hospital HMI evidence for the affected station/rack/zone: whether two AGVs appear under one rack/zone or whether an AGV appears in an unexpected location
Any visible tote association indicators on hospital HMI (if exposed)
If authorization/visibility is available: backend state evidence from the approved read-only procedure(s) supporting AGV/location/tote context
Record evidence without making state changes
nodes.healthy_interpretation: AGV position and station/rack association match the expected layout and no disconnected/orphaned tote association is observed.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: An AGV is displayed in an unexpected location; duplicate occupancy under one rack/zone is shown; and/or a tote appears associated with a removed/disconnected AGV.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Hospital view identifiers cannot be read (low resolution); the association cannot be confirmed; or the anomaly is based only on second-hand discussion.
nodes.generated_guidance: Use this node to confirm that the suspected mismatch is actually present before attempting any recovery. If you cannot uniquely identify the affected station/AGV/tote from available evidence, stop into the escalation gate rather than mutating state.

evidence_collection_procedures.title: Use AGV API Controls to Remove/Recover an AGV and Pause/Resume All AGVs
evidence_collection_procedures.purpose: Use the System HMI API screen’s AGVs section to remove a problematic AGV by ID, recover (add back) the AGV by ID after physical recovery, and pause/resume all AGV movement fleet-wide.

evidence_collection_procedures.title: Start OptiSweep AGV System (Reset Metrics → Start System → Close Out/Bag Out → Verify Running → Shut Down)
evidence_collection_procedures.purpose: Perform the required AGV start-up prerequisites (nine empty AGVs: five under the north rack and four under the south rack), start the OptiSweep system 15 minutes before the sort, run the documented start sequence (Reset Metrics → Start System → Close Out/Bag Out), verify the system returns to the "Running" state after Bag Out, and then shut down.

evidence_collection_procedures.title: Start OptiSweep AGV System From Shut-down Mode (Reset Metrics → Start → Close out/Bag Out → Running)
evidence_collection_procedures.purpose: Use the OptiSweep system screen to bring the AGV system from Shut-down Mode into the normal “Running” state by verifying the required number of empty AGVs, resetting metrics, starting the system, performing close out (Bag Out) until the system returns to “Running,” and then shutting down when finished.

nodes.title: Validate hospital tote flow and AGV recovery
nodes.intent: Confirm that the hospital station accepts totes again and that the affected AGV and tote state no longer prevents normal flow.
nodes.goal: Confirm that the hospital station accepts totes again and that the affected AGV and tote state no longer prevents normal flow.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to validate hospital-station tote add and remove behavior, confirm the affected AGV roster or location state through the source-evidenced hospital or AGV view, and monitor for continued backlog or recurrence before declaring the hospital flow recovered.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source reports restoration of adding and removing totes and that all robots were re-added and running.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to validate hospital-station tote add and remove behavior, confirm the affected AGV roster or location state through the source-evidenced hospital or AGV view, and monitor for continued backlog or recurrence before declaring the hospital flow recovered.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site operator observes the hospital station and performs the approved validation activity. Healthy signal: totes can be added and removed at the hospital, AGVs are re-added or operating as expected, and movement resumes. Unhealthy signal: tote addition remains unavailable, an AGV remains shut down or misplaced, or backlog continues to grow. Inconclusive: only a general statement that the system is running is available without a hospital-specific tote-flow check.

unhealthy_indicators: Hospital still cannot accept or induct totes.

nodes.intent: Hand off when the hospital tote or AGV state cannot be safely identified or the approved correction does not restore hospital tote flow.
nodes.goal: Hand off when the hospital tote or AGV state cannot be safely identified or the approved correction does not restore hospital tote flow.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to prepare an escalation handoff containing hospital HMI or layout evidence, AGV and tote association observations, API dog or Aveva action results, validation results, and clear stop criteria; the handoff procedure must identify the role authorized to continue.
nodes.source_supported_description: The packet documents uncertain cause, unreadable artifacts, and high-level state-correction actions without a complete supported procedure.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to prepare an escalation handoff containing hospital HMI or layout evidence, AGV and tote association observations, API dog or Aveva action results, validation results, and clear stop criteria; the handoff procedure must identify the role authorized to continue.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: L1/L2 support observes that the evidence is insufficient, the authorized interface cannot complete the supported correction, or hospital validation remains unsuccessful. Healthy signal for this gate is not recovery; it is a documented stop condition with sufficient evidence for the next role. Unhealthy continuation signal: further unapproved state changes, physical handling, or database changes would be required.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The packet contains an annotated hospital-area HMI-style layout used in the investigation.
The source describes using Aveva for AGV and tote state correction.

healthy_indicators: Stop condition satisfied: sufficient evidence exists for an escalation handoff; no further state changes performed here.
unhealthy_indicators: Supported correction cannot be completed or validated.
Further action would require unauthorized physical, database, or configuration changes.
inconclusive_indicators: The affected AGV, tote, or station cannot be uniquely identified.
Evidence is limited to second-hand reports or unreadable screenshots.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: Do not treat the source's suspected removed-AGV explanation as confirmed diagnosis.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Incident summary states the exact cause was not known and lists several recovery actions.

nodes.primary_action: Stop and prepare an escalation handoff only after confirming that hospital tote/AGV state cannot be safely identified or that the supported correction did not restore hospital tote flow.
evidence_to_collect: Hospital HMI/layout evidence of the attempted/observed induction failure context
AGV and tote association observations (what is known vs unknown)
Results of any attempted authorized corrections via Apidog/WCS API (success/reject/uncertain post-action state)
Validation results from hospital tote add/remove behavior
Stop criteria justification: why further state-changing or physical actions would be unsafe or unapproved
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Gate condition is met as a stop/handoff event with sufficient evidence for the next role; no additional unapproved state changes should be performed here.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Attempting additional unapproved physical/database/config changes would be required to continue without evidence or authorization.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Affected AGV/tote/station cannot be uniquely identified or evidence is limited to second-hand/unreadable artifacts.
nodes.generated_guidance: Do not treat the suspected removed-AGV explanation as confirmed diagnosis. The handoff must include what evidence was available and what could not be verified.

playbooks.title: Site cannot start or sustain sort
playbooks.user_facing_summary: Troubleshoot a broad operational outage where the site cannot start sort or stops during sort, with possible server or service abnormality and subsequent recovery validation.
playbooks.playbook_goal: Determine whether the report represents a site-wide sort availability problem, assess the source-supported service or server recovery direction, and validate stable operation without treating the historical service hypothesis as confirmed cause.

nodes.source_supported_description: The source reports that the site was down and could not start sort or went down in the middle of sort; the associated dashboard screenshot is not readable enough to interpret independently.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to confirm with the site whether sort is unavailable across the operation, whether movement stopped or only the hospital flow is affected, and whether the available site status or dashboard view shows a readable down or running state; do not infer the meaning of unreadable color cells.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site operator reports whether sort cannot start or stopped during operation and whether movement is broadly affected; the source-evidenced status screenshot or site operational view is checked only for readable overall state. Healthy signal: sort starts and continues with normal movement. Unhealthy signal: site is down, sort cannot start, or sort stops broadly. Inconclusive: the screenshot is unreadable or the report is limited to one station or one AGV.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: Teams messages state that the site was down and could not start sort or went down during sort.

ontology_gaps: The supplied ontology snippets do not establish a mapping for the unreadable status dashboard or a specific site-wide sort-state backend model.
healthy_indicators: Site reports sort starts and remains active.
Movement is occurring across the affected operation.
unhealthy_indicators: Site is reported down.
Sort cannot start or stops in progress.
Broad movement is absent.
inconclusive_indicators: Only a localized hospital or AGV issue is reported.
The dashboard screenshot has no readable labels or legend.
The report is second hand and cannot be reproduced.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Site was reported down and could not start sort or went down during sort.

nodes.primary_action: Confirm with the site whether sort is unavailable site-wide (and whether broad movement is absent), and treat any unreadable dashboard colors as un-interpretable until readable operational state is provided.
evidence_to_collect: Site operator statement on whether sort cannot start, stops broadly during operation, or is limited to a hospital-station symptom
Readable overall site operational state evidence provided by the site (not inferred from unreadable color-only dashboard cells)
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Sort starts and continues with normal movement across the operation (not just a single hospital station).
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: The site is down, sort cannot start, or sort stops broadly with movement broadly absent.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: The dashboard/screenshot is unreadable (no interpretable legend/labels), or the report is limited to one station/one AGV and cannot establish site-wide impact.
nodes.generated_guidance: Do not infer meaning from unreadable color cells. If the site cannot provide readable overall status, branch to inconclusive and avoid assuming the outage is site-wide beyond the evidence.

ontology_evidence.title: WCS model — SystemDatabaseModel
ontology_evidence.text: Model SystemDatabaseModel (robotics): System state and current sort GUID.. Fields: Id: Row id.; EntityInserted: Insert timestamp.; EntityLastUpdate: Last update timestamp.; Status: System status enum.; SortGuid: Current sort GUID. Select template (catalog_derived): SELECT TOP (1000) [Id], [EntityInserted], [EntityLastUpdate], [Status], [SortGuid] FROM [Helix2x_1Prod_Robotics].[dbo].[SystemDatabaseModel]

ontology_evidence.title: Capability — Fleet / overall system status
ontology_evidence.text: Capability fleet_system_status: Confirm overall fleet / system-down vs running from overview surfaces.. When: Blank RMS, site-wide stoppage report, overall system page down. Not for: Single-AGV active error deep dive without overall context.. Surfaces: rms_ui, aveva_hmi, event_viewer, wcs_sql, site_interview. Support contract: {}. Backend mappings: []. DBs: robotics, sorter_sweeper. Models: SystemDatabaseModel, SystemStateModel, SortModel. APIs: SystemState. Key fields: SystemDatabaseModel.Id: R

ontology_evidence.title: Capability — AGV active errors
ontology_evidence.text: Capability agv_active_errors: Confirm whether AGVs/robots currently have active error or fault state.. When: Site reports AGV stopped, alarms, bump, path lost, or software showing robot faults; corroborate RMS overview vs WCS truth. Not for: Physical bump recovery steps (use agv_physical_recovery); Ignition OPC alone; tote NoRead.. Surfaces: rms_ui, wcs_sql, wcs_api, site_interview, apidog. Support contract: {}. Backend mappings: []. DBs: robotics, sorter_sweeper. Models: AgvActiveErrorDatabaseM

nodes.intent: Determine whether the broad outage correlates with the documented AGV hospital-station server or service abnormality.
nodes.goal: Determine whether the broad outage correlates with the documented AGV hospital-station server or service abnormality.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to inspect the AGV hospital-station server or OptiSweep service state using the named service evidence available in the case, including Windows Services or Event Viewer only if the current diagnostic artifact identifies those views, and to distinguish a live service fault from a historical notes entry.
nodes.source_supported_description: The case artifacts and closure details mention AGV hospital-station server issues, services needing reset, and later reset of OptiSweep services, but do not show the live service state or exact service names.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to inspect the AGV hospital-station server or OptiSweep service state using the named service evidence available in the case, including Windows Services or Event Viewer only if the current diagnostic artifact identifies those views, and to distinguish a live service fault from a historical notes entry.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: L1/L2 support inspects the documented service/server evidence and any available named service view. Healthy signal: relevant services are responsive and no abnormal condition is observed. Unhealthy signal: the named incident context continues to show a server or service abnormality, or service responsiveness is absent. Inconclusive: the packet provides only a notes entry saying services need reset and no live service state or exact service name is available.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The packet labels the AGV repair artifact as a Windows-services-related screenshot, although enrichment notes that the visible crop is a notes pane rather than a live Services console.

ontology_gaps: The packet does not identify exact OptiSweep service names or provide a validated event-log mapping.
The artifact is a notes pane rather than proof of a live Windows Services state.
healthy_indicators: Relevant service or server state is responsive.
No current service abnormality is observed in the available named view.
unhealthy_indicators: AGV hospital-station server is reported as having service issues.
OptiSweep services are reported as requiring reset or are not responsive.
inconclusive_indicators: Only a historical work-order note is available.
Exact service names and live state are unavailable.
The dashboard or service artifact cannot be read.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: AGV hospital station is described as having server issues and needing services reset.
Resolution details state that Opti sweep services were reset.

nodes.primary_action: Inspect the documented OptiSweep/AGV hospital-station server or related service evidence to determine whether the abnormality is live (responsive issues) versus only a historical work-order note.
evidence_to_collect: Windows Event Viewer / Services evidence relevant to OptiSweep and/or WCSWebApplication failures (including whether services are running/stopped and whether there are abnormal crash/restart patterns)
Any live host/service responsiveness evidence that distinguishes current fault from historical 'needs reset' notes
If exact service names are not available, capture what is identifiable in the artifact and what is missing
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Relevant services/host state are responsive and no current abnormal condition is observed in the evidence you can inspect.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: The evidence indicates a live service/server abnormality consistent with the outage symptom (e.g., stopped services or crash/restart abnormality).
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Only a historical notes/work-order entry is available; exact service names or live state cannot be confirmed from the available artifact(s).

optional_corroboration.note: If only RMS indicates issues while service evidence is unclear, corroborate by attempting WCS/SQL/API-backed service-health evidence available in the environment (only if accessible and relevant).

nodes.generated_guidance: The packet indicates the visible artifact may be a notes pane rather than a live Windows Services console, so rely on Event Viewer/Services evidence to establish current state and avoid treating the closure note as proof of an active fault.

nodes.expected_or_observed_result: L1/L2 support or the authorized site role observes that the approved service recovery or Hospital Lane restart has completed. Unhealthy signal: the recovery is rejected, the service remains abnormal, or the action would affect an unsafe or unknown operational state. healthy_indicators: Authorized recovery is completed.
Service or Hospital Lane responsiveness returns.
Movement begins again.
unhealthy_indicators: Service remains unavailable or the lane does not recover.
Recovery causes or reveals additional AGV, tote, or safety anomalies.
inconclusive_indicators: Recovery completion is reported without a direct operational observation.
No authorized role is available to perform the supported recovery.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: Do not infer that resetting services is safe or sufficient without the approved procedure and role authorization.

nodes.trigger_condition: L1/L2 support or the authorized site role observes that the approved service recovery or Hospital Lane restart has completed. Progress signal: service responsiveness or lane availability returns. Unhealthy signal: the recovery is rejected, the service remains abnormal, or the action would affect an unsafe or unknown operational state. Inconclusive: completion is asserted but no observable service, lane, or movement change is available.
nodes.failure_boundary: Stop at the documented failure condition and escalate; do not invent a recovery path.

nodes.title: Validate stable sort and movement recovery
nodes.intent: Confirm that the site can start or sustain sort and that movement remains active after service or lane recovery.
nodes.goal: Confirm that the site can start or sustain sort and that movement remains active after service or lane recovery.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to validate OptiSweep or service responsiveness, confirm Hospital Lane and site sort operation, observe sustained movement, and check for recurrence after recovery; the validation procedure should define the monitoring interval and evidence to retain without prescribing exact screen navigation.
nodes.source_supported_description: The packet reports that movement started and the system was running, while the earlier symptom was inability to start or sustain sort.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to validate OptiSweep or service responsiveness, confirm Hospital Lane and site sort operation, observe sustained movement, and check for recurrence after recovery; the validation procedure should define the monitoring interval and evidence to retain without prescribing exact screen navigation.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site operator observes sort startup and continued movement, while support verifies any available named service or operational status view. Healthy signal: sort starts, movement is active, and the site remains running. Unhealthy signal: sort cannot start, the site goes down again, or movement stops. Inconclusive: a general message says the system is running but no sustained sort or movement observation is available.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: Teams messages report that movement started and that the system was running.
The resolution path names Hospital Lane as part of recovery.

ontology_gaps: The supplied ontology does not provide a detailed mapping for sustained sort validation or the specific Hospital Lane status.
healthy_indicators: Site reports sort started successfully.
Movement is occurring and remains active.
System is reported running after recovery.
unhealthy_indicators: Sort cannot start.
Sort stops again after recovery.
Movement does not resume or quickly stops.
inconclusive_indicators: Only a single 'system is running' message is available.
No direct observation of sustained sort or movement is available.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: If broad sort availability is not restored or stability cannot be demonstrated, use the escalation gate rather than declaring recovery.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Chat reports that movement started and the system was running.

nodes.primary_action: Validate stable sort and movement recovery after service/lane recovery by confirming sort startup, continued movement, and absence of immediate recurrence.
evidence_to_collect: Operator confirmation that sort started successfully and continues
Operator observation that movement remains active over a monitoring interval (to detect quick stop/recurrence)
Support-side verification using any available named operational status/service view (if accessible)
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Sort starts and remains active; movement is active and the site remains running/stable after recovery.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Sort cannot start, stops again after recovery, or movement does not resume / quickly stops.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Only generic 'system is running' message is available; insufficient evidence of sustained sort or movement.

optional_corroboration.note: If sustained movement evidence is hard to obtain, corroborate with any available overall system/roster fault overview that can distinguish running vs stopped state.

nodes.generated_guidance: Validation should include sustained monitoring rather than a single confirmation message; a quick stop indicates unhealthy recovery.

nodes.goal: Hand off when the service or server condition cannot be confirmed, authorized recovery does not restore operation, or the site remains unable to start or sustain sort.

nodes.source_supported_description: The source contains incomplete service evidence, an unreadable dashboard artifact, and a site-wide outage that eventually recovered through multiple actions.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to prepare escalation evidence including service or server observations, Event Viewer or Windows Services evidence when available, sort availability reports, Hospital Lane state, recovery actions attempted, and validation results, with stop criteria and the receiving technical role.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: L1/L2 support observes unresolved service abnormality, failed recovery, repeated outage, or insufficient evidence to continue safely. Healthy signal for this gate is a complete evidence package and controlled handoff, not continued troubleshooting. Unhealthy continuation signal: repeated resets, unsupported changes, or declaring recovery from a single unverified status message.

healthy_indicators: Evidence package complete; controlled handoff to L2/L3 ready.
unhealthy_indicators: Sort remains unavailable after the supported recovery path.
The site repeatedly goes down or cannot start sort.
Further recovery would require unsupported or unauthorized changes.
inconclusive_indicators: Only an unreadable dashboard or historical notes entry is available.
The service name or current state cannot be identified.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: Historical unfamiliarity, support participation, and communication delays are not themselves escalation conditions; escalation is based on unsafe, unsupported, or unresolved technical state.

nodes.primary_action: Stop and prepare a controlled handoff to L2/L3 when service recovery or sustained sort validation cannot be confirmed; compile evidence and ensure receiving role has what is needed to proceed safely.
evidence_to_collect: Sort availability/sort-start and sustained movement results (site reports)
Service/server observations attempted and their outcomes (Event Viewer / Windows Services if available)
Hospital Lane state evidence (where available) and recovery actions attempted
Any recurrence signals and why further recovery would be unsafe/unsupported
nodes.healthy_interpretation: A complete evidence package is produced and the handoff is controlled (no further unsupported troubleshooting).
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Sort remains unavailable after supported recovery attempts or evidence is insufficient and continued changes would be unsafe/unauthorized.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Only unreadable dashboard or historical notes are available and current service name/state cannot be identified; evidence package must be completed as best as possible.
nodes.generated_guidance: This node is a stop condition; do not declare success from a single unverified status message. Escalate based on unresolved technical state or insufficient evidence to continue safely.

ontology_evidence.evidence: Escalation depends on unresolved service/server abnormality or inability to confirm it with Windows service/event evidence.
